* docs: replace stylized benchmark numbers in README with real measured values

Numbers now sourced from packages/ouroboros-integrations/bench-data.json
(N=10,000, mulberry32-seeded, Node 24.0.0):

- Dual-witness clean 100% / noisy 43.6% at tau=0.40

commit.message:
fix(r3): explicit permissions: {} to resolve Scorecard Token-Permissions finding (#18)

Replaces the comment-only omission of workflow-level permissions with
an explicit empty grant. Resolves the OpenSSF Scorecard alert
'TokenPermissionsID: no topLevel permission defined' that was flagged
on this repository's scorecard.yml after the R2 read-all removal.

Empty {} keeps the same effect (no clamping of job-level write scopes
needed by the Scorecard reusable workflow) while satisfying the
Token-Permissions check that requires the block to be present.

Verified rationale: api.securityscorecards.dev currently scores this
repo 6.4 (as of 2026-05-10) with this finding open.
This fix targets the high-severity TokenPermissionsID instance
attached to .github/workflows/scorecard.yml:1.

commit.message:
fix(ci): remove workflow-level 'read-all' that blocks Scorecard startup (#16)

The reusable Scorecard workflow needs job-level 'security-events: write' and
'id-token: write'. A workflow-level 'permissions: read-all' was clamping the
job to read-only and producing startup_failure with no analysable logs.
Job-level grants alone are sufficient and follow least-privilege at the job
boundary.

commit.message:
chore(security): SHA-pin reusable workflow refs to .github@c8359e5 (#14)

Round-2 audit: reusable workflow consumers were referencing
`szl-holdings/.github/.github/workflows/*.yml@main` (mutable). Repins to
the current main commit on the org .github repo so this consumer is
immune to upstream branch tampering.

When the upstream reusables are intentionally updated (new Node version,
new lint rule), Dependabot will open a PR to bump this SHA — same flow as
any other action pin.

Signed-off-by: Stephen Lutar <stephenlutar2@gmail.com>
